name: clawmetry-setup-openclaw
description: Pinned OpenClaw CLI for the setup-openclaw composite action. CI-only: nothing here ships in the clawmetry wheel or is imported by the dashboard.
//overrides: The openclaw pin is held by ONE remaining blocker, not the two first
recorded here. See the note on this directory's Dependabot entry in
.github/dependabot.yml. `npm audit fix` still resolves every finding here
by bumping openclaw, and that is still not a bare version change.
Re-measured 2026-10-02 against openclaw 2026.9.7, by regenerating the
lockfile from this package.json with only the version changed and keeping
the overrides below as they are. Reproducible from the steps named.
1. THE ADVISORY TRADE NOW FAVOURS THE BUMP. It did not in September.
3 advisories before, all high (openclaw <=2026.6.5-beta.6,
extract-zip, @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent <=0.78.1); 3 after,
2 high + 1 moderate, no critical. All three current highs clear.
The 2026-09-22 figures that used to stand here -- 4 vulnerable
packages / 26 advisories BEFORE to 16 / 67 AFTER at 2026.5.27,
gaining a critical (tar GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw) -- do NOT reproduce at
2026.9.7. The overrides below have been extended since, and the
top-level copies stay patched through the bump: brace-expansion
5.0.12, ip-address 10.7.2, and openclaw's own undici 8.10.2.
The 3 that remain are NOT clearable from this file at any openclaw
version. 2026.9.7 takes `npm` 11.20.0 as a direct dependency, and all
three resolve under node_modules/npm/node_modules/ with
`inBundle: true` (brace-expansion GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr, undici
GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r, ip-address GHSA-j6r3-76f7-8jcv). `overrides`
cannot rewrite a package manager's bundled dependencies.
2. THE SQLITE TRANSCRIPT BOUNDARY IS CLEARED. OpenClaw moved per-session
<sid>.jsonl transcripts into agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite,
and the daemon only globbed agents/main/sessions/*.jsonl, so a bump
past that boundary took the live E2E suites red. #6233 shipped
clawmetry/openclaw_sqlite.py, which reads that store read-only and
mirrors it into the JSONL layout the daemon already ingests; its
CHANGELOG entry records a verified daemon ingest of a live OpenClaw
boundary hunt that used to be written here is moot.
3. THE ONE BLOCKER LEFT IS NODE, and it is new. 2026.9.7 declares
engines.node ">=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0". The action's `node-version`
default is the bare major "22", which no longer satisfies that range
(the older note here said it did, measured against 5.27's >=22.19.0).
No workflow in this repository sets up Node 24: nine are on "20",
three on "22". So moving the pin is a Node major move for every
setup-openclaw caller -- ci.yml, e2e-nightly.yml,
moat-keystone-drive-nightly.yml, openclaw-boot.yml and
oss-golden-path.yml, plus clawmetry-cloud's own copy of the action in
cloud-e2e-screenshots.yml. Raise the default and the E2E fleet moves
with it; that is the decision this pin now waits on.
These overrides take the subset of that fix that does NOT require moving
openclaw: each is a patch/minor bump inside the major the tree already
resolves, so no consumer sees a new API surface. Keys are range-scoped
(name@major) deliberately -- a bare `undici` key would also rewrite the
undici@7.29.1 that @earendil-works/pi-ai resolves, which IS a major bump.
tar@7    7.5.15 / 7.5.13 -> 7.5.22  clears GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw (critical),
GHSA-8x88-c5mf-7j5w, GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m,
GHSA-vmf3-w455-68vh, GHSA-w8wr-v893-vjvp,
GHSA-gvwx-54wh-qm9j
undici@8 8.2.0 -> 8.10.2            clears GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g and the ten
other 8.x advisories
ws@8     8.20.0 -> 8.21.3           clears GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p, GHSA-58qx-3vcg-4xpx
markdown-it@14                      clears GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq
brace-expansion@5                   clears GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 (high),
5.0.9 -> 5.0.12            GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p (high), GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr
fast-uri@3  3.1.7 -> 3.1.8          clears GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj
ip-address@10                       clears GHSA-j6r3-76f7-8jcv, GHSA-h3mg-xc3c-68pw
markdown-it was previously listed below as uncoverable, on the grounds that
its only fix was 15.x. That is no longer true: upstream backported the
smartquotes fix into the 14 line (14.3.1, then 14.3.2, both published after
15.0.2). The advisory range is <=14.1.1, so 14.3.2 is out of range while
staying inside the major the tree already resolves -- the same shape as the
three overrides above, and no new API surface for any consumer.
What these deliberately do NOT cover, because no override can:
extract-zip      GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv and GHSA-7pqw-9j4j-h8q3 have no fixed
release; 2.0.1 is latest and is itself in range.
pi-coding-agent  0.79.0 clears all four advisory ranges, but overriding to
it is a net regression -- measured, see below. And no
LATER version can be taken either: 2026-09-27 established
that as an API-contract break, not arithmetic. See (2) at
the end of this note before trying it.
openclaw itself  19 advisories, fixed across 2026.5.18..2026.6.5. Every
one is fixed only by the version bump.
pdfjs-dist used to be listed here ("fix is 6.2.108, a major bump from the
5.7.284 in tree"). It is now taken as a deliberate exception -- see (1) at
the end of this note.
Those stay open against the pin. Re-confirmed 2026-09-22: extract-zip is
still 2.0.1 (published 2020, latest, in range).
The pi-coding-agent line above previously read that 0.74.2 was "the only
release between the pinned 0.74.0 and the openclaw bump", so a later
release could not help. That was wrong on the facts -- 0.78.0 (2026-05-29),
0.78.1 (2026-06-04) and 0.79.0 (2026-06-08) all predate it, and three of
the four advisories are ranged >=0.74.0 <0.78.1 with the fourth <0.79.0, so
0.79.0 is outside all four. The conclusion was still right; the reason was
not. Corrected here so the next reader does not re-derive it, or ship the
regression on the strength of the advisory ranges alone.
MEASURED 2026-09-24 by adding `"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "<v>"` to
the overrides below, regenerating the lockfile with nothing else changed,
and running `npm audit` (`npm install --package-lock-only`):
0.74.0 (the pinned resolution)   4 packages / 26 advisories  4 high
0.78.1                           7 packages / 40 advisories  6 high, 1 mod
0.79.0                           7 packages / 39 advisories  6 high, 1 mod
Both are the SAME failure mode as blocker 1 above, one layer down. openclaw
2026.5.12 depends on pi-coding-agent at exactly 0.74.0, whose tree hoists to
the root where the range-scoped keys match. 0.78.1 and 0.79.0 instead nest
their own copies under node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/ --
undici@8.3.0, ws@8.20.1, brace-expansion@5.0.6, protobufjs@7.5.9 -- where
the keys do not match, so those four come back vulnerable while the root
overrides go on holding harmlessly. On top of that, both versions land
INSIDE a newer pi-coding-agent advisory range (<=0.83.0) that 0.74.0 sits
outside of, so the override trades four known advisories for a fifth plus
the four un-overridden transitives.
So: no pi-coding-agent override, and the four advisories stay open against
the pin. A range-scoped key cannot reach a nested copy; only re-deriving
this whole block against the nested tree can, which is blocker 1's work
and wants doing once, for openclaw and pi-coding-agent together.
These advisories are the WHOLE of what OSSF Scorecard reports as this
repository's VulnerabilitiesID. Before 2026-09-27 that was 26: 19 openclaw,
4 pi-coding-agent, 2 extract-zip, 1 pdfjs-dist. The pdfjs-dist one is now
cleared, leaving 25. Nothing else in the repo contributes one, so a reader
chasing that score is looking at this pin and nowhere else.
They close when BOTH blockers above clear: the overrides re-derived against
the nested tree, and the daemon able to read the OpenClaw SQLite transcript
if the pin moves past 2026.5.28..2026.6.34.
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-27. Two conclusions, one of which overturns nothing and
one of which makes the pi-coding-agent line above PERMANENT rather than
merely measured. Read the second before trying that override again.
1. pdfjs-dist@5 -> 6.2.108 is now taken, and it is the one override here
that does NOT obey the 'patch/minor inside the major already resolved'
rule the other four follow. 6.2.108 is the first release outside
GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j (range >=5.6.83 <6.2.108), so there is no in-major
fix to take. It carries @napi-rs/canvas 0.1.100 -> 1.0.9 (pdfjs 6.x's
optional native canvas) and re-nests pi-coding-agent under
node_modules/openclaw/ instead of hoisting it; verified that the four
root overrides still resolve to the same versions and that no new
vulnerable transitive appears. Accepted because this tree is CI-only and
nothing in CI opens a PDF: the advisory is arbitrary JS execution on
opening a malicious one. If the desktop or wheel ever vendored this
tree, re-derive rather than inherit this call.
2. THE pi-coding-agent OVERRIDE CANNOT BE TAKEN AT ANY VERSION while the
openclaw pin is 2026.5.12, and the advisory arithmetic above is not the
reason. It was tried at 0.87.1 (chosen because it is outside the
<=0.83.0 range that made 0.78.1 and 0.79.0 a net regression, and because
by advisory count it looks like a clear win: 4 packages / 26 advisories
/ 4 high down to 1 / 19 / 1, dropping extract-zip out of the tree
entirely). It does not work. openclaw 2026.5.12 imports AuthStorage from
this package -- see dist/pi-model-discovery-*.js, reached from
commands-handlers and context -- and 0.87.1 no longer exports it. The
gateway starts its HTTP server, then dies:
SyntaxError: The requested module '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'
does not provide an export named 'AuthStorage'
0.74.0 exports it; 0.87.1 does not. So this is an API-contract break, not
a dependency-hygiene tradeoff, and no advisory-clean version can be
assumed safe: the export set is what has to match, and only the openclaw
bump moves both sides together. That is blocker 1's work, as above.
HOW THAT WAS MISSED, so the next reader does not repeat it: `npm ci`
succeeds and `openclaw --version` prints 2026.5.12 (f066dd2) with the
broken override in place. Neither loads the module graph that imports
AuthStorage. The gate that catches it is booting the gateway, which is
what .github/workflows/openclaw-boot.yml does and what caught this:
openclaw gateway --port 18789 --verbose --allow-unconfigured
# then poll http://127.0.0.1:18789/ for any HTTP response
It reproduces locally in about five seconds and logs 'http server
listening (7 plugins...)' when the tree is sound. Run it, not just
--version, for ANY change to this file's overrides or lockfile.
Net effect of the one override taken: 4 packages / 26 advisories / 4 high
-> 3 / 25 / 3 high. The 25 that remain are 19 openclaw, 4 pi-coding-agent
and 2 extract-zip, so the Scorecard paragraph above now reads 25, not 26.
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-30. Three advisories were published against packages
already in this tree at versions that used to be clean: brace-expansion
(two high, one moderate), fast-uri (one moderate) and ip-address (two
moderate). They are added to the override table above rather than left
open, because all three are the easy shape -- each resolves to exactly one
copy at the ROOT of the hoisted tree (node_modules/<name>, `npm audit`
effects: []), which is where a range-scoped key matches, and each fix is a
patch inside the major already resolved. That is the same case as tar,
undici, ws and markdown-it, and it is only available while the openclaw pin
is 2026.5.12: blocker 1 above is precisely that a bump re-nests these under
node_modules/openclaw/ and puts them back out of reach.
Measured by regenerating the lockfile with only these three keys added
(`npm install --package-lock-only`) and running `npm audit`:
before  6 packages / 31 advisories  4 high, 2 moderate
after   3 packages / 25 advisories  3 high
No new vulnerable transitive appears, and the five overrides already here
still resolve to the same versions (tar 7.5.22, undici 8.10.2, ws 8.21.3,
markdown-it 14.3.2, pdfjs-dist 6.2.108) -- checked, because re-resolving is
exactly what blocker 1 warns can silently stop them matching. The undici
7.29.1 under @earendil-works/pi-ai is untouched, which is the reason these
keys are range-scoped and not bare.
That returns the tree to the 3 / 25 / 3 high steady state the paragraph
above describes, and the 25 are again exactly 19 openclaw + 4
pi-coding-agent + 2 extract-zip -- the three uncoverable packages. The
Scorecard VulnerabilitiesID paragraph is accurate again as written.
Boot gate run for this change, per the instruction above -- `openclaw
gateway --port 18789 --verbose --allow-unconfigured`, polled until it
answered: HTTP 200, 'http server listening', 'ready', on OpenClaw 2026.5.12
(f066dd2). `npm audit fix` is still not available to us; nothing here moves
the openclaw pin.
RE-MEASURED 2026-10-01. A newly published advisory, basic-ftp
GHSA-c475-qrg2-pj4r (high, quadratic-time CPU denial of service in the
Unix directory-listing parser, range <=6.2.0), landed against a package
already in this tree at a version that used to be clean -- the same shape
as the 2026-09-30 batch. It is added to the table above rather than left
open, but it is the FIRST entry here that needs a BARE key, so read the
next paragraph before touching it.
basic-ftp  5.3.1 -> 6.2.1  clears GHSA-c475-qrg2-pj4r (high)
WHY THE KEY IS BARE, against the range-scoped rule stated above. The
scoped form `basic-ftp@5` was tried first and is WRONG here: it matched
only one of the two requesters, which de-hoisted the package and left the
root copy vulnerable while adding a second, patched copy under
node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/. Measured -- the tree stayed at 8
packages / 26 advisories with basic-ftp still listed at 5.3.1. A bare key
cannot over-reach in this particular case, which is what makes it safe:
before this change the tree held exactly ONE basic-ftp, at the hoisted
root (node_modules/basic-ftp, 5.3.1), requested by get-uri@8.0.0 (^5.2.0)
and by the get-uri@6.0.5 nested under pi-ai (^5.0.2). Both ranges are 5.x,
so there is no second major for a bare key to rewrite. That is the
opposite of the undici case the rule was written for, where a bare key
would also have caught the undici@7.29.1 under pi-ai. Re-check that
single-copy fact before copying this key form to anything else.
This one also does NOT obey the 'patch/minor inside the major already
resolved' rule, for the same reason pdfjs-dist does not: the advisory
range is <=6.2.0, which covers every 5.x release, so no in-major fix
exists and 6.2.1 is the first version outside it. Unlike pdfjs-dist it is
not accepted on CI-only grounds -- the major was checked against the
consumer that actually calls it. get-uri calls exactly five Client
methods (access, close, downloadTo, lastMod, list). All five carry
byte-identical signatures in 5.3.1 and 6.2.1, and dist/index.d.ts exports
the same names in both; what the major actually changed is internal (a
new TransferWatchdog, plus FtpContext/transfer/netUtils). Verified at
runtime after npm ci: get-uri imports, all five methods are present on a
basic-ftp 6.2.1 Client, and the patched parser still parses an ordinary
Unix listing. The fix itself is an anchor on the listing regex.
Measured by regenerating the lockfile with only this key added
(`npm install --package-lock-only`) and running `npm audit`:
before  8 packages / 26 advisories  8 high
after   3 packages / 25 advisories  3 high
The before figure is 8 rather than the 3 the paragraphs above describe
because this one advisory cascaded: basic-ftp -> get-uri ->
pac-proxy-agent -> proxy-agent -> pi-ai and openclaw all appeared as
vulnerable via that chain, none of them with an advisory of their own.
Clearing the root collapses all five. The lockfile change is three lines;
nothing re-nested and no new package entered the tree. All eight
pre-existing overrides still resolve to the same versions (tar 7.5.22,
undici 8.10.2, ws 8.21.3, markdown-it 14.3.2, brace-expansion 5.0.12,
fast-uri 3.1.8, ip-address 10.7.2, pdfjs-dist 6.2.108) -- checked,
because re-resolving is exactly what blocker 1 warns can silently stop
them matching -- and the undici 7.29.1 under pi-ai is untouched.
That returns the tree to the 3 / 25 / 3 high steady state, and the 25 are
again exactly 19 openclaw + 4 pi-coding-agent + 2 extract-zip, the three
uncoverable packages. The Scorecard VulnerabilitiesID paragraph above is
accurate as written.
